newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Hewlett Packard plans 1,000 new Irish jobs.
newsitem.headline: Hewlett Packard plans 1,000 new Irish jobs.

text.p: Hewlett Packard Co, the U.S. multi-national high-technology electronics group, on Thursday said it was creating 1,000 new jobs at its Leixlip plant in Co. Kildare as part of a 100 million punt expansion plan.
Hewlett Packard, which located in Ireland in 1977, is estimated to have invested a total 420 million Irish pounds in its Irish operation.

"This is phase three, which is an expansion of our final assembly operation," human resources manager Kevin McNamara told Reuters. "You are talking about circa 1,000 jobs being created out to about 2001 and this will bring the total 3,000 people."

Hewlett Packard said the expansion, which will involve the assembly of ink-jet printers, is a response to worldwide demand for such printers, driven by the growth in colour printing and increasing use of the Internet.
"We are expanding because of the sales boom of ink-jet printers which we supply," McNamara said. "We sell to markets all around the world with a large supply going to Europe."
Last week technology group Seagate Technology Inc announced that it also planned to create 1,000 new jobs in its southern Irish facility in Cork.
